category_feedback.specific_evidence: recovery_moves is terse three-item list: 'Count by 5s.', 'Use chart.', 'Compare values directly.' No branching by what the diagnostic showed and no research citation. Trap is real but Level 4 needs branched recovery and named research.
category_feedback.required_fix: Branch recovery_moves: (a) if child skip-counts but doesn't connect to value, line 5 nickels under 1 quarter and match physically; (b) if can't skip-count, drop to one-cent counting; (c) if reverts on next pair, do 3 paired examples. Cite Sowder unit-coordination or Carpenter & Moser CGI grouping research.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Penny is quoted twice but no distinctive quotable refrain reused in consolidation. exit_routine is a generic frame '___ is ___ than ___' with no character chant. Cassie appears only in hook with no consistent voice across lesson segments.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a memorable Penny refrain children chant at consolidation, e.g. 'COUNT the VALUE, not the COINS!' repeated across Lessons 4-5. Have Cassie echo with a complementary line. Use the refrain in worksheet header so the chant carries between lesson and independent practice.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression solid and count-vs-value trap is named, but children don't compare strategies (teacher scripts only skip-count by 5s), and common_misconceptions is plain-language ('Count = value. Repair: count value.') with no research-grounded framing.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a 60-second 'how did you figure it out?' share-out where 2-3 pairs name different strategies (skip-count by 5s; group as quarters; one-for-one match). Name the misconception in expanded_walkthrough.rationale as 'unit-coordination failure' citing Steffe & Cobb on units or Sowder on number sense.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet parts each map to a success criterion and image_assets reference Penny+Cassie. But the worksheet doesn't deliberately introduce a transfer item flagged as a generalization probe; it mirrors the lesson's compare format directly without varying the practice format.
category_feedback.required_fix: Flag the Part 1 item '5 nickels vs 1 quarter' explicitly in teacher_notes as a count-vs-value transfer probe so teachers watch for that misconception. Add a Part 4 mini-challenge '4 quarters vs 1 loonie' (equal) to test transfer of equivalence. Document transfer rationale in teacher_notes.

summary: Strong G1 F1.1 compare-values lesson with the count-vs-value trap correctly identified. Falls short of the high bar with four categories at 3 (ped_depth, voice, math_auth, consistency). Lesson-side fixes (branched recovery + research citation + Penny refrain + strategy share-out) lift three categories together; worksheet needs only a minor transfer-task tweak.
